Runtime and identity keep separate two-connection pools and existing authorization/leases. APIs only enqueue. Suspend the document cron before shared execution; email cron is unaffected. No requirement for three separately hosted workers.
targetArchitecture.consistency: Never mark a source sync successful before its data commits. Resume checkpoints after failures. Manual daytime imports still need downstream linkage/review reconciliation.
targetArchitecture.documents: Shared cooldown, source dedup and daily admission are deployed; all five flags including bounded rechecks and health logs were observed enabled. The 22 October audit confirms first-night discovery progress, not cache savings or an exercised recheck. Rechecks use existing quota/headroom/window limits. Metadata TTL alone does not schedule rechecks or delete old metadata.
targetArchitecture.freshnessTradeoff: Nightly automatic imports mean Xero changes can remain invisible until the next successful night. Explicit manual refresh remains available. Do not call the local view live Xero data.

Idle client connections are retained for 60 seconds rather than the installed pg-pool default of 10 seconds. SOPHIA_RUNTIME_DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS can override this within 1-300 seconds. Maximum pool size is unchanged.
Timing headers and logs distinguish new/reused client acquisition and record total/idle/waiting counts before acquisition. The metadata and combined access-query durations have their own metrics.
